item.title: Google Stock Gets Another Bullish Signal From US Courts
item.description: Google was accused of having an illegal advertising monopoly. On Wednesday, it still walked away with the business intact. US District Judge Leonie Brinkema
item.dc:creator: BeInCrypto
item.content:encoded: Google was accused of having an illegal advertising monopoly. On Wednesday, it still walked away with the business intact. US District Judge Leonie Brinkema rejected the Justice Departments attempt to force Google to sell AdX, the exchange at the heart of its advertising system. Alphabet shares rose modestly after the breakup threat disappeared. Instead, Brinkema ordered changes to how Google operates its ad tools, including giving rivals greater access to bidding data. A Narrow Escape for Google? The case began in 2023, when the Justice Department and several states accused Google of dominating the technology publishers use to sell online ads. In April 2025, Brinkema agreed. She found Google had illegally tied publishers to AdX, where it collects a 20% fee. substantially harmed Googles publisher customers, the competitive process, and, ultimately, consumers of information on the open web, Reuters reported, citing Brinkema. Google argued that selling AdX would be technically difficult and disruptive for customers. The judge rejected the breakup. The ruling extends a striking pattern. Exactly one year earlier, another judge allowed Google to keep Chrome. Meta then kept Instagram and WhatsApp in November. US regulators have now lost three straight attempts to break up Big Tech. Ad Manager itself is small beside Alphabets $4.08 trillion valuation. It generated 4.1% of Googles revenue and 1.5% of operating profit in 2020. Google Stock Performance. Source: Google Finance The pressure has hardly disappeared. Google still faces regulatory problems in Europe, while its AI position remains less settled and Alphabets huge AI spending is becoming a bigger question for investors. Read the article at BeInCrypto

item.title: Citi partners with FAB, OCBC for live payments pilot on Swift blockchain ledger
item.description: Citigroup teamed with Swift, First Abu Dhabi Bank, OCBC to run live USD transactions on Swift’s blockchain-based ledger. Move targets always-on, cross-bord
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Citigroup teamed with Swift, First Abu Dhabi Bank, OCBC to run live USD transactions on Swift’s blockchain-based ledger. Move targets always-on, cross-border payments using tokenized deposits, aiming to cut cut-off constraints, speed beneficiary credit, improve liquidity efficiency. Pilot phase runs from July to December 2026; similar transactions planned later this month with DBS, UOB. Effort aligns with Citi Services’ digital-asset push across payments, securities, collateral; Citi Token Services processes about USD 1 billion in transactions. item.title: Sector Update: Financial Stocks Higher Late Afternoon
item.description: 03:44 PM EDT, 09/02/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Financial stocks were advancing late Wednesday afternoon, with the NYSE Financial Index adding 1% and the State S
item.dc:creator: MT newswire
item.content:encoded: 03:44 PM EDT, 09/02/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Financial stocks were advancing late Wednesday afternoon, with the NYSE Financial Index adding 1% and the State Street Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLF) up 0.9%. The Philadelphia Housing Index increased 0.6%, and the State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLRE) was shedding 0.7%. Bitcoin (BTC-USD) was declining 0.2% to $77,230, and the yield on 10-year US Treasuries was steady at 4.796%. In economic news, ADP's monthly measure of private payrolls showed a 38,000 rise in August, below a 47,000 gain expected in a Bloomberg survey, following a 46,000 increase in July. New orders for US factory goods rose by 0.9% in July, above expectations for a 0.7% increase in a survey compiled by Bloomberg and following a 0.2% decrease in June. In corporate news, Capital One Financial (COF) was pressed by Democratic Senator Maggie Hassan for details about an internal anti-money laundering review that the bank said last month had led to the closure of accounts tied to President Donald Trump and his businesses, Reuters reported Wednesday, citing a letter sent by the senator to Capital One CEO Richard Fairbank Tuesday. Capital One shares were up 2.8%. KKR (KKR) has agreed to buy residential garage door repair and replacement company A1 Garage Door Service for about $2 billion, Reuters reported. KKR shares rose 0.9%. TPG (TPG) has filed a confidential application to list hospital assets worth nearly $8 billion in Malaysia, The Wall Street Journal reported. TPG shares added 0.4%. Citigroup's (C) Citibank NA London Branch has been fined about 4.7 million British pounds ($6.3 million) under the UK's Russia sanctions regime, Britain's Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation said. Citi shares were up 1.4%.

item.title: Provident Financial FY26 net income rises 6% to $6.7 million; net interest margin widens 16 basis points to 3.09%
item.description: Provident Financial Holdings posted net income of $6.7 million, up 6% from the prior fiscal year; diluted EPS rose to $1.03. Net interest income climbed 2%
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Provident Financial Holdings posted net income of $6.7 million, up 6% from the prior fiscal year; diluted EPS rose to $1.03. Net interest income climbed 2% to $36.3 million; net interest margin widened 16 basis points to 3.09%. Total interest expense fell 8% to $19.6 million, led by a 22% drop in borrowing costs to $7.7 million. Non-interest income increased 6% to $3.7 million; other non-interest income rose 19% to $873,000 on a Visa share conversion gain. Total assets slipped 3% to $1.21 billion; deposits rose 2% to $910.4 million while borrowings dropped 26% to $157 million.
